chunks: Sulaymān ibn Khālid said to al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام: “May I be your ransom, inform me about the obligations that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has imposed upon the servants—what are they?” He said:

“Testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, establishing the five salats (prayers), giving zakat, performing the hajj to the House, fasting the month of Ramaḍān, and the wilayah.”
So whoever upholds them, acts correctly, keeps close to the right course, and avoids every evil shall enter Paradise.

key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: the obligatory alms-tax due on qualifying wealth
key_terms.الْجَنَّةَ: Paradise, the final reward for obedience
key_terms.الْفَرَائِضِ: the obligatory duties imposed by Allah upon His servants
key_terms.الْوَلَايَةُ: the divinely ordained authority and guardianship associated with the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ: the pilgrimage to the Sacred House
key_terms.شَهَادَةُ: the testimony of faith affirming Allah’s oneness and the Messengership of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.صِيَامُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: fasting during the month of Ramaḍān

ai.seo_question: What obligations does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام list as the fundamental duties of a Muslim?
ai.summary: This hadith lists the foundational obligations imposed by Allah upon His servants: the shahadah, salat, zakat, hajj, sawm of Ramadan, and wilayah. It presents these duties together as the essential framework of faith and worship, and promises jannah for the one who upholds them and avoids evil.
